history.summary: The Bhudhara Chandi Temple is an ancient shrine of Goddess Chandi on Bhudhara Pahada (Bhudhara hill) at Sajanagarh, near Nilagiri, in Balasore district. Maa Bhudhara Chandi is worshipped as the Grama Devi (guardian goddess) believed to protect the land and its people, with strong tribal participation from villages around Nilagiri, Sajanagarh and Mayurbhanj. The temple is built in the Kalinga style of Odisha with a curvilinear deula (tower); the inner sanctum enshrines Goddess Chandi. It is best known for the annual Uda Parba festival (around Raja, 15 June) featuring Hakanda Puja, the Nian Pata fire-walking ritual, and traditional tribal dances and songs. CSV town correction: the temple is NOT in Balasore town - it stands at Sajanagarh in the Nilagiri area of Balasore district. Identity is moderately supported by travel and review sources, but no scholarly history is available. Note: a Wanderlog listing shows the place as 'permanently closed' as of 2026 - verify on the ground whether the shrine is active (the Uda Parba festival videos are from recent years, suggesting continued worship).

town_description: Sajanagarh is a village near Nilagiri in Balasore district, Odisha, in the forested Nilagiri hill region. It is known as the seat of Maa Bhudhara Chandi, the guardian Grama Devi of the area, and for the Uda Parba festival with its fire-walking ritual.
